Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 W.P.No.20095 of 2024
O R D E R:

Heard learned counsel for petitioner through Video Conference mode, learned Assistant Government Pleader attached to the Office of the learned Advocate General appearing for respondent Nos. 1 to 5, and perused the record.

entities.text: Office of the learned Advocate General
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that though the respondents-authorities have initiated land acquisition proceedings by issuing preliminary notification, dt.27.01.2022 gazetted on 29.01.2022,
no award has been passed till date; that she was issued with notice, dt.27.01.2024, under Section 21 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act'); that she had submitted objections to the aforesaid notice on 27.01.2024 stating that her name has been excluded in the preliminary notification issued by the respondents-authorities in respect of land in survey No.302 of Sha Nagar Village, Ramadugu Mandal, Karimnagar District, though the same was proposed to be acquired for the purpose of excavation of Main Canal-III between IFFC & Kakatiya Canal; and that in spite of the petitioner submitting her objections to the aforesaid acquisition proceedings, no action has been initiated and no award has been passed till date correcting the name of the enjoyer of the land in survey No.32 of S h a N a g a r V i l l a g e , R a m a d u g u M a n d a l , K a r i m n a g a r D i s t r i c t , a n d i n s t e a d t h e respondents-authorities are continuing land acquisition proceedings in the name of wrong person,
which action it is contended as illegal and arbitrary.
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Petitioner further contends that since, the land acquisition proceedings were initiated by issuing preliminary notification under Section 11(1) of the Act on 27.01.2022 published on 29.01.2022, the acquisition proceedings have lapsed, and thus, the respondents-authorities cannot proceed with the land acquisition proceedings.
4. Counter affidavit on behalf of respondent No.4 is filed.

By placing reliance on the aforesaid counter affidavit, learned Assistant Government Pleader would submit that though the preliminary notification was gazetted on 29.01.2022, the validity of the said notification was extended by further period of 12 months and thereafter declaration u/s.19 of the Act was published on 24.01.2024 and gazetted on 25.01.2024; that the authorities thus, have time of one year for passing an Award from the date of the gazette notification of the declaration; and that since, the said period of 12 months has not lapsed, the petitioner cannot claim of the respondents-authorities not passing an award and the preliminary notification having lapsed.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader would further submit that the Declaration under Section 19 of the Act was published in Eenadu vernacular newspaper and Hindu newspaper on 03.02.2024 and also published the substance in the locality on 27.01.2024.

6. Learned Assistant Government Pleader would further submit that the authorities on obtaining extension and publishing the declaration under Section 19 of the Act on 25.01.2024 have issued notice under Section 21 of the Act to the petitioner on 27.01.2024.
7.

It is further contended by the learned Assistant Government Pleader that on the authorities issuing the aforementioned notice under Section 21 of the Act, petitioner having submitted objections to the same on 27.01.2024, the authorities would consider the said objections while passing the Award by causing enquiry in terms of Section 23 of the Act; and that during the said enquiry, if the authorities find the claim of the petitioner to be valid and genuine, the authorities would consider the same, and if the authorities notice existence of any dispute in relation to the subject land, they would take further action as provided under the Act at the time of passing of the Award.
8.
I have taken note of the respective submissions made.

9. Though the petitioner had claimed that due to non-passing of the Award by the respondents-authorities, the preliminary notification having lapsed, it is to be noted that since, the respondents by the counter affidavit filed have stated the authorities obtaining extension of time as provided under Section 19(7) of the Act by publishing a declaration on 25.01.2024, the authorities would get a further period of 12 months from the date of declaration for passing of the award as per Section 25 of the Act, which is yet to expire.
10.

Thus, the eventualities contemplated either under Section 19 or Section 25 having not occurred,
the petitioner cannot claim that the preliminary notification having lapsed, thereby the respondents-authorities being precluded from taking any action in respect of the land being claimed by the petitioner.

11. Further, it is to be noted that on the respondents-authorities issuing preliminary notification on 27.01.2022 published on 29.01.2022, the petitioner was required to submit objections thereto within 60 days.
Admittedly, the petitioner did not submit objections within the time provided under Section 11(4) of the Act.

Since, no objections were received, the authorities took further action of issuing a declaration under Section 19 of the Act on 25.01.2024, after obtaining extension as provided under the Act, and thereafter have issued notice under Section 21 of the Act on 27.01.2024.

12. It is at this point, the petitioner submitted her objections to the notice issued under Section 21(4)
of the Act, which is required to be gone into by the respondents-authorities while undertaking award enquiry in terms of Section 23 of the Act.

13. Since, it is stated that the authorities are in the process of award enquiry, this Court is of the view that the respondents- authorities are to be directed to consider the objections submitted by the Parlapelli Leya vs State Of Telangana on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66994845/
2 petitioner on 27.01.2024 while passing the Award in terms of Section 25 of the Act.

sentences.text:
Upon the respondents-authorities passing the Award, if the claim of the petitioner is accepted, she would be entitled to receive the compensation determined thereunder, failing which, the authorities are at liberty to make a reference to the Authority under Section 64 of the Act.
14.
Subject to the above directions, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
15. Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in these writ petitions shall stand closed.
T. VINOD KUMAR, J 07th January, 2025.
